BURHAN:v4p266/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p266/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p266/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the second thumma in the repeated curse as making the second denunciation more emphatic than the first.
BURHAN:v4p266/r5.anchor: قلت الدلالة على إن الكرة الثانية من الدعاء ابلغ من الاولى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r1.claim: The burden of the Day of Judgement weighs on the sky, which may split and reveal the Day suddenly while people remain heedless; 7:187 likewise says it burdens heaven and earth and comes suddenly.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r1.anchor: The heavens and the earth are burdened with it. It will come upon you suddenly.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r2.claim: Although only God knows the Hereafter’s time, its signs are obvious like a pregnancy near delivery, so it may arrive at any time.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r2.anchor: everyone who sees her knows that she will deliver

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r3.claim: People are unfortunate to ignore the Hereafter merely because its exact arrival time is unknown.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r3.anchor: Unfortunate are people who are indifferent to it merely because its exact time of arrival is not known to them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.claim: The arrogant Quraysh leader fashioned a disdainfully delivered excuse, misjudging the Qur’an as a prophet’s stirring eloquence and ignoring its warning, though its statements are realities he will soon meet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.anchor: they reckoned it to be a miracle of a prophet’s stirring and eloquent speech and never paid attention to its warning

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p44/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p44/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p44/r2.claim: He delays his reaction after hearing the Qur'an so onlookers will think their leader is considering it seriously.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r1.claim: After pondering, he carefully weighed his opinion so that his words would take root with listeners and appear credible.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r1.anchor: he thoroughly weighed the opinion that came to his mind

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r3.claim: The phrase إنه فكر explains the threat that he would be burdened, or it may replace the description of him as obstinate and explain his plotting; he considered the Qurʾān and its messenger, then weighed what to say.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r3.anchor: إنه فكر: تعليل للوعيد في قوله: سأرهقه صعودا

SAMIN-DURR:74:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:18/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:18/r1.claim: إنه فكر may be an independent explanatory sentence for سأرهقه.
SAMIN-DURR:74:18/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون استئناف تعليل لقوله " سأرهقه "

SAMIN-DURR:74:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:18/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:18/r2.claim: Alternatively, إنه فكر is a substitute for إنه كان لآيتنا عنيدا.
SAMIN-DURR:74:18/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بدلا من { إنه كان لآيتنا عنيدا }

ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r3.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r3.claim: Al-Walid asks Meccan leaders what they will say about Muhammad when people ask, after noting the spread of his message.
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r3.anchor: وكان الوليد بن المغيرة قال لرؤساء أهل مكة، قد رأيتم هذا الرجل

ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r4.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r4.claim: When leaders propose calling Muhammad mad, al-Walid rejects it because anyone who spoke with him would recognize that he was not mad.
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r4.anchor: قالوا نقول: هو مجنون، قال: إذن يخاطبوه فيعلموا أنه غير مجنون.

ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r5.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r5.claim: He rejects calling Muhammad a poet because Arabs know poetry and know his message is not poetry; he rejects ‘soothsayer’ because Muhammad says ‘if God wills.’
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r5.anchor: قالوا: فنقول إنه كاهن، قال الكهنة لا تقول إنه يكون كذا وكذا إن شاء الله وهو يقول إن شاء الله

ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r6.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r6.claim: After reflection, al-Walid calls Muhammad's message sorcery learned from Musaylima and the people of Babylon.
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r6.anchor: ففكر وعبس وجهه وبسر، أي نظر بكراهة شديدة. فقال: ما هذا الذي أتى به محمد إلا سحر يأثره عن مسيلمة وعن أهل بابل.

ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r7.speaker: أبو جهل
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r7.claim: Abu Jahl tells his uncle that people say he has apostatized and that they plan to gather wealth for him in exchange for what he might take from Muhammad's followers.
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r7.anchor: وجاء أبو جهل ابن أخيه، فقالوا: إن القوم يقولون إنك قد صبوت.

ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r8.claim: Al-Walid replies that they will never satisfy him, asks how he could take their money, and says he is among the wealthiest people.
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r8.anchor: فقال: والله ما يشبعون، فكيف أقدر أن آخذ منهم مالا وإني لمن أيسر الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v29p123/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123/r1.claim: The clause may explain his deserving the threat, or explain his hostility to God’s signs; on the latter reading it is explanatory and has no syntactic position.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123/r1.anchor: تعليل للوعيد واستحقاقه له أو بيان لعناده لآياته عز وجل فيكون جملة مفسرة لذلك لا محل لها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p123/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123/r2.claim: Another parsing makes the clause an appositional replacement for “he was hostile to Our signs”: he thought about what to say concerning the Qurʾān and decided on his words.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123/r2.anchor: وقيل الجملة عليه بدل من قوله تعالى أنه لآيا عنيدا أي أنه فكر ماذا يقول في شأن القرآن وقدر في نفسه ما يقول

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r1.claim: As context, the Prophet recited Ghāfir 40:1–3 in the mosque while al-Walīd listened; he repeated it when he noticed him. Walīd praised its sweetness, beauty, and force as neither human nor jinn speech.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r1.anchor: وذلك أن الله تعالى لما أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم "حم تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم" إلى قوله: "المصير" (غافر: 1-3)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r2.speaker: قريش
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r2.claim: Quraysh said Muhammad bewitched Walīd and feared the tribe would follow; Walīd was their prized one.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r2.anchor: فقالت قريش: [سحره محمد] (4) [صبأ والله الوليد، والله لتصبون قريش كلهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r3.speaker: أبو جهل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r3.claim: Abū Jahl says Quraysh is gathering money for Walīd because they think he praised Muhammad for food; Walīd says he is wealthy and Muhammad's companions have no surplus food.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r3.anchor: فقال لهم أبو جهل: أنا أكفيكموه فانطلق فقعد إلى جنب الوليد حزينا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r4.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r4.claim: Walīd rejects claims Muhammad is mad, soothsayer, poet, or liar; Muhammad had been called al-Amīn before prophethood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r4.anchor: تزعمون أن محمدا مجنون، فهل رأيتموه يخنق قط؟ قالوا: اللهم لا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r5.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r5.claim: Asked what Muhammad is, Walīd reflects and calls him a sorcerer whose speech separates families and allies.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r5.anchor: فما هو؟ فتفكر في نفسه ثم نظر ثم عبس، فقال: ما هو إلا ساحر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r6.claim: He thought about Muhammad and the Qurʾān and deliberated what accusation to make against them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p268/r6.anchor: فذلك قوله عز وجل: {إنه فكر} في محمد والقرآن {وقدر} في نفسه ماذا يمكنه أن يقول

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:18-19/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:18-19/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:18-19/r1.claim: The phrase either explains the man's defiance or gives its cause: he contrived in his mind what to say against the Qurʾān.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:18-19/r1.anchor: تعليل أو بيان للعناد، والمعنى فكر فيما يخيل طعنا في القرآن

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:18-19/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:18-19/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:18-19/r3.claim: A report says al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra heard the Prophet recite Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda and praised its eloquence, but after Abū Jahl provoked him he called it magic for dividing families; Quraysh rejoiced. No grading is stated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:18-19/r3.anchor: روي أنه مر بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقرأ { حم } «السجدة»

BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r1.claim: The obstinate man repeatedly turned the thought over, following his desire to find an accusation against the Qur’an.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r1.anchor: ردد فكره وأداره تابعا لهواه لأجل الوقوع على شيء يطعن به في القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r2.claim: He weighed possible attacks on the Qur’an within himself to decide which came closest to a plausible thing to say.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r2.anchor: أوقع تقديرا للأمور التي يطعن بها فيه وقاتيها في نفسه ليعلم أيها أقرب إلى القول

BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r3.claim: His thinking led others into ruin by barring faith, and brought him lasting destruction that deprived him of beneficial life in both worlds.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r3.anchor: تفكيره وتقديره قد أوقع غيره في الهلاك بمنعه من حياة الإيمان أصيب هو بما منعه من حياة نافعة في الدارين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r3.claim: His obstinacy was his effort to discredit the Qur’an as magic, poetry, or soothsaying despite knowing it was none of these.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r3.anchor: هو محاولته الطعن في القرآن وتحيله للتمويه بأنه سحر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r4.claim: The threat is parenthetical between the account of his obstinacy and his thought, hastening warning for his distress and comfort for the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r4.anchor: قصد بهذا الاعتراض تعجيل الوعيد له مساءة له وتعجيل المسرة للنبيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r5.claim: His thinking and devising explains and completes the statement that he was obstinate toward God’s signs.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p406/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p406/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p406/r1.claim: He thought over what to say about the Quran and weighed the statement within himself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p406/r1.anchor: أي تفكر ماذا يقول في القرآن وقدر القول في نفسه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r1.claim: Al-Walid pondered what to say about the Quran and deliberated over an invented claim; Ibn Kathir links his punishment to distance from faith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r1.anchor: أي: إنما أرهقناه صعودا، أي: قربناه من العذاب الشاق؛ لبعده عن الإيمان، لأنه فكر وقدر، أي: تروى ماذا يقول في القرآن حين سئل عن القرآن،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r9.claim: The man is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, a Quraysh leader.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r9.anchor: وهذا المذكور في هذا السياق هو: الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، أحد رؤساء قريش

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that al-Walid first praised the Quran as neither poetry, magic, nor madness but God’s speech; after Abu Jahl’s pressure he called it transmitted magic.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: دخل الوليد بن المغيرة على أبي بكر بن أبي قحافة فسأله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r2.claim: Ikrima reports al-Walid softened on hearing Muhammad recite; Abu Jahl manipulated him into denouncing it, and he eventually called it learned magic.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة: أن الوليد بن المغيرة جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرأ عليه القرآن، فكأنه رق له.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq and other historians report a similar account.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر محمد بن إسحاق وغير واحد نحوا من هذا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says Quraysh’s council debated calling Muhammad poet, magician, soothsayer, or madman to deter pilgrims; al-Walid then chose the charge of transmitted magic.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r4.anchor: وقد زعم السدي أنهم لما اجتمعوا في دار الندوة ليجمعوا رأيهم على قول يقولونه فيه، قبل أن يقدم عليهم وفود العرب للحج

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r10.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r10.claim: Qatada reports that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira judged the Qur'an neither poetry nor ordinary speech: it was sweet, beautiful, overpowering, and must be magic; this is what he considered and calculated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r10.anchor: قال قتادة : زعموا أن الوليد بن المغيرة قال : لقد نظرت فيما قال هذا الرجل فإذا هو ليس بشعر , وإن له لحلاوة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r11.claim: Al-Mawardi allows that al-Walid reflected on his hostility and calculated how to wage it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r11.anchor: ويحتمل وجها ثالثا : أن يكون فكر في العداوة وقدر في المجاهدة

BURSEVI:v10p176#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p176#2/r10.speaker: تاج المصادر
BURSEVI:v10p176#2/r10.claim: The cited lexicon glosses tafkir as thinking or reflecting.
BURSEVI:v10p176#2/r10.anchor: بمعنى التفكر والتأمل كما قال في تاج المصادر التفكير انديشه كردن

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#7/r1.claim: His plotting explains the threat: God hastened poverty and humiliation after his wealth and honor, and will punish his extreme defiance with severe afterlife torment for calling the Qurʾān magic.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#7/r1.anchor: تعليل للوعيد كان الله تعالى عاجله بالفقر والذل بعد الغنى والعز لعناده ويعاقبه في الآخرة بأشد العذاب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#7/r2.claim: He thought about what to say concerning the Qurʾān, then devised and prepared his words.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#7/r2.anchor: يعني أنه فكر ماذا يقول في القرآن ﴿ وقدر ﴾ في نفسه ما يقوله وهيأه

QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: he considered the Prophet and Quran, then prepared words to say; Arabic qaddartu means I prepared something.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r1.anchor: يعني الوليد فكر في شأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والقرآن و «قدر» أي هيأ الكلام في نفسه،

QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r2.claim: After hearing Quran 40:1–3 from al-Walid, Quraysh feared he had accepted it. Abu Jahl provoked him by alleging he was accused of praising Muhammad for food; al-Walid denied needing money, rejected the usual charges against Muhammad, then called him a sorcerer because he divided families and allies.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r2.anchor: وذلك أنه لما نزل: حم * تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم [غافر: 1]إلى قوله: { إليه المصير } سمعه الوليد يقرؤها

QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r3.claim: The repeated words mean that al-Walid considered what to say about Muhammad and the Quran, then calculated a charge to make.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r3.anchor: فذلك قوله تعالى: { إنه فكر } أي في أمر محمد والقرآن { وقدر } في نفسه ماذا يمكنه أن يقول فيهما.

RAZI-FULL:v30p176#5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#5/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#5/r1.claim: To think or reflect is to examine and deliberate over a matter.
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#5/r1.anchor: فكر في الأمر وتفكر إذا نظر فيه وتدبر

RAZI-FULL:v30p176#5/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#5/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#5/r2.claim: After reflecting, he arranged words in his heart and prepared them; this is what “he determined” means.
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#5/r2.anchor: ثم لما تفكر رتب في قلبه كلاما وهيأه وهو المراد من قوله : { فقدر }

TAB-FULL:v23p428/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that al-Walid first told Quraysh the Qur'an was God's speech, not poetry, magic, or madness; fearing his conversion, Abu Jahl shamed him into calling it magic acquired from others, and the passage was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنه فكر وقدر} [المدثر: 18] إلى {ثم عبس وبسر} [المدثر: 22] قال: دخل الوليد بن المغيرة على أبي بكر

TAB-FULL:v23p431/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r1.claim: Qatada reports al-Walid saying the Qur'an was not poetry, had sweetness and surpassing beauty, yet must be magic; he then frowned and grimaced, prompting the curse in the verse.
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إنه فكر وقدر} [المدثر: 18] زعموا أنه قال: والله لقد نظرت فيما قال هذا الرجل

TAB-FULL:v23p431/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the one who thought and calculated as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira at Dar al-Nadwa.
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {فكر وقدر} [المدثر: 18] قال: الوليد بن المغيرة يوم دار الندوة

TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the solitary one as al-Walid, whom Muhammad invited to Islam; after delaying, considering, frowning, turning away, and calling the message magic, he was consigned to Saqar.
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} [المدثر: 11] يعني الوليد بن المغيرة دعاه نبي الله

TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd recounts that al-Walid examined Muhammad reciting in prayer, called the speech sweet and heart-gripping, rejected poetry and soothsaying, then allowed that it might be magic transmitted from earlier people.
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا وجعلت له مالا ممدودا} [المدثر: 12] إلى قوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r1.claim: Fakkara means to consider and deliberate over a matter.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r1.anchor: يقال: فكر في الأمر، وتفكر، إذا نظر فيه وتدبر (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r2.claim: Qaddara likewise means to estimate or calculate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r2.anchor: يقال: فكر في الأمر، وتفكر، إذا نظر فيه وتدبر (¬8)، ومثله:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r3.speaker: مقاتل وعكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r3.claim: Maqātil and ʿIkrima report that al-Walīd heard the Prophet recite 40:1–3 and praised the speech as unlike human or jinn speech, sweet, elegant, and surpassing; Quraysh said he had converted, so Abū Jahl confronted him, after which al-Walīd called the speech sorcery.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r3.anchor: هذا قول مقاتل (¬5)، وعكرمة (¬6). وقال الكلبي:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī gives another account: at the pilgrimage gathering al-Walīd advised Quraysh how to answer questions about Muḥammad, rejecting claims of madness, poetry, or soothsaying as easily disproved; Abū Jahl then accused him of converting for food, and al-Walīd concluded the Qurʾān was sorcery.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: كان الوليد بن المغيرة قال لرؤساء مكة: إن الناس مجتمعون بالموسم غدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says al-Walīd thought about the Qurʾān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد في القرآن (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r6.claim: Maqātil says he thought about Muḥammad and privately calculated what he would say about him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p425/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: في محمد، وقدر مع نفسه ماذا يقول له (¬6)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#6/r1.claim: The man considered and plotted against Muhammad and his message, alternately calling him a poet, magician, or soothsayer, among similar accusations.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#6/r1.anchor: في كيد محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وما جاء به، فقال: "شاعر" مرة، و "ساحر" مرة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p446/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p446/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p446/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that al-Walid heard the Quran and praised its sweet, forceful language as unlike poetry, but after Abu Jahl pressed him to denounce Muhammad he called it transmitted magic; verses 74:11–24 were revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p446/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أن الوليد بن المغيرة جاء إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقرأ عليه القرآن وكأنه رق له، فبلغ ذلك أبا جهل،

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p447/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p447/r1.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p447/r1.claim: Mujahid reports al-Walid's deliberation and his eventual charge that the Quran was magic, after rejecting Quraysh's claims that Muhammad was mad, a soothsayer, poet, or liar.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p447/r1.anchor: وقال مجاهد: إن الوليد بن المغيرة كان يغشى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأبا بكر - رضي الله عنه - حتى حسبت قريش أنه يسلم،

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r16.claim: Al-Walīd reportedly convened Quraysh leaders, considered the Prophet and Quran, ruled out possession, soothsaying, poetry, and lying, then concluded Muhammad must be a sorcerer.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r16.anchor: It is reported that al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah called together all of the leaders of the Quraysh and asked them about the Prophet

TABATABAI:74:12-25/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r7.claim: Fikr is thinking; taqdīr arranges meanings and qualities mentally by order, precedence, affirmation, and negation to reach a desired conclusion.
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r7.anchor: التفكير معروف، والتقدير عن تفكير نظم معان وأوصاف في الذهن بالتقديم والتأخير والوضع والرفع

TABATABAI:74:12-25/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r8.claim: Al-Walid sought a claim that would undermine the Qurʾan and satisfy its hostile opponents; after considering poetry, soothsaying, madness, and fables, he chose magic because it divides families and allies.
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r8.anchor: وقد كان الرجل يهوى أن يقول في أمر القرآن شيئا يبطل به دعوته ويرضي به قومه المعاندين

TABRISI:74:11-31/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:11-31/r1.claim: A report recounts that Muhammad recited 40:1–3 in the mosque while al-Walid ibn al-Mughira listened, repeated the passage when he noticed, and al-Walid praised its sweetness and power.
TABRISI:74:11-31/r1.anchor: قام إلى المسجد والوليد بن المغيرة قريب منه يسمع قراءته فلما فطن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:74:11-31/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31/r2.speaker: أبو جهل
TABRISI:74:11-31/r2.claim: Quraysh feared al-Walid would convert and others follow; Abu Jahl prompted him to dismiss Muhammad’s speech, and al-Walid called it sorcery because it divides families.
TABRISI:74:11-31/r2.anchor: فقالت قريش صبأ والله الوليد والله لتصبأن قريش كلهم

TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r13.claim: He pondered and planned what to say about the Qurʾān, but did so to contrive falsehood; seeking guidance by thought would instead be praiseworthy.
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r13.anchor: ودبر ماذا يقول في القرآن { وقدر } القول في نفسه وإنما فكر ليحتال به للباطل

THALABI:v10p71/r23.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p71/r23.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p71/r23.claim: Al-Walid heard Muhammad recite the opening of Ghafir in the mosque, then praised the Qur'an's sweetness, beauty, fruitfulness, and supremacy.
THALABI:v10p71/r23.anchor: إنه فكر وقدر الآيات، وذلك أن الله سبحانه لما أنزل على النبي (عليه السلام) حم تنزيل الكتاب

ELMALILI:74:14-25/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r11.claim: The verse explains the threat's cause or his obstinacy: al-Walid thought and made a mental estimate, measuring and guessing.
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r11.anchor: ve bir takdir yaptı zihninde ölçtü biçti, bir tahmin yaptı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r1.claim: A report says the polytheists asked al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra how to respond to Muhammad and the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r1.anchor: Rivayete göre müşrikler Hz. Peygamber’e ve tebliğ ettiği Kur’an’a karşı nasıl bir tavır takınmaları gerektiğini Velîd b. Mug^re’ye sormuşlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r2.claim: After deliberating, al-Walīd advised them to call Muhammad a magician and the Qur’an inherited magic and human speech.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r2.anchor: o da düşünüp taşındıktan sonra Hz. Peygamber’in bir sihirbaz, Kur’an’ın da önceki sihirbazlardan intikal eden bir sihir, bir beşer sözü olduğunu insanlar arasında yaymalarını tavsiye etmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.claim: Verses 18–25 condemn people who, like al-Walīd, adopt a similar unbelieving posture toward the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.anchor: İşte 18-25. âyetlerde Velîd b. Mug^re örneğinde Kur’an’a karşı benzer şekilde inkârcı tutum sergileyenler kınanmış

FARRA:v3p202/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p202/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p202/r1.claim: When Meccan leaders debated what to tell pilgrims, al-Walid rejected calling Muhammad mad, poet, or soothsayer; after deliberation he chose to call him a sorcerer.
FARRA:v3p202/r1.anchor: فهذا تفسير قوله: «إنه فكر وقدر» القول فى محمد صلى الله عليه

NAHHAS:v5p67/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p67/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p67/r1.claim: The man who pondered and schemed is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, without disagreement; he repeatedly considered how to refute God's signs.
NAHHAS:v5p67/r1.anchor: أي فكر في رد آيات الله جل وعز وقد رجع مرة بعد مرة ينظر هل يقدر أن يردها

NAHHAS:v5p67/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p67/r2.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v5p67/r2.claim: Qatāda reports that al-Walīd considered the Prophet's message, called it neither poetry nor ordinary speech, then described its sweetness and elegance as magic.
NAHHAS:v5p67/r2.anchor: قال قتادة زعموا أنه فكر فيما جاء به النبي فقال والله ما هو بشعر

ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r3.claim: On hearing the messages, he reflects on how to disprove them, destroys himself by that deliberation, looks for arguments, frowns, then turns away and glories in arrogance.
ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r3.anchor: he reflects and meditates [as to how to disprove them]

DURR-FULL:v8p327/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p327/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p327/r11.claim: Qatada recounts that al-Walid considered Muhammad’s words sweet, beautiful, fruitful, and dominant, yet concluded they were magic; the condemnation from how he measured through becoming sullen was revealed about him.
DURR-FULL:v8p327/r11.anchor: عن قتادة {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} قال: هو الوليد بن المغيرة

DURR-FULL:v8p330/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p330/r2.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p330/r2.claim: Mujahid reports Ibn Abbas saying al-Walid canvassed Quraysh’s views, rejected poetry and soothsaying based on his expertise, then reflected and called the message magic passed on from others.
DURR-FULL:v8p330/r2.anchor: من طريق مجاهد عن ابن عباس قال: لما بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جمع الوليد بن المغيرة قريشا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r20.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r20.claim: Exegetes relate that al-Walid heard and admired the Quran, nearly accepted Islam, and visited Abu Bakr; Abu Jahl then warned that Quraysh reproached him and urged him to say something pleasing to them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r20.anchor: روى جمهور المفسرين أن الوليد سمع من القرآن ما أعجبه ومدحه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r2.speaker: الزهري وجماعة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r2.claim: Al-Zuhri and others report that al-Walid praised the Quran's sweetness, deep roots, fruitful branches, force, and inimitable height, then rejected labels of poetry, soothsaying, and madness before conceding it resembled magic.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r2.anchor: وروي عن الزهري وجماعة غيره أن الوليد حاج أبا جهل وجماعة من قريش في أمر القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r9.claim: A report says the Prophet summoned al-Walid and told him to look and think; after thinking, he gave the quoted judgment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r9.anchor: وقد روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا الوليد

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.claim: The passage is said to concern al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, wealthy with sons and called al-Wahid among his people, according to Ibn Amir.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.anchor: قيل: نزلت هذه الآيات في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، وكان له مال وبنون، قال ابن عامر: وكان يسمى الوحيد في قومه،

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.claim: In the story, al-Walid rejects calling Muhammad a soothsayer, poet, or madman, then chooses “magician” and says the Qur’an separates families.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.anchor: ثم اختلفوا، فقيل: إنه أتى قريشا في ناديها، وقال: هذا الموسم، والناس يسألون عن محمد،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r3.claim: His extreme hostility, culminating in calling the Qur'an magic, explains the threat and brought loss after wealth and humiliation after honor.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r3.anchor: لبلوغه بالعناد غايته وأقصاه في تفكيره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r5.claim: Alternatively, إنه فكر is an appositive explanation of إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r5.anchor: بدلا من قوله : { إنه كان لاياتنا عنيدا } بيانا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r6.claim: He considered what to say about the Qur'an and prepared his words.

MUQATIL:74:18-30/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r1.claim: Al-Walid considered Muhammad's case, claimed he was a sorcerer, and reckoned that Muhammad divided people from one another.
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r1.anchor: في أمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فزعم أنه ساحر
